h1: Aluminum & PVC window and door machinery — welding, cleaning, machining, assembly and complete lines
intro: Window and door shops turn PVC (vinyl) and aluminum profiles into frames in a set order: cut, machine the hardware places, weld or crimp the corners, clean the welds, mill the mullion ends, cut the glazing beads and assemble. NovoTech supplies the machines for every step from Plastmak, built in Bursa, Turkey: single-, double- and 4-corner PVC welders and CNC corner cleaners; a 9-axis profile machining centre, 3-axis CNC drilling and milling machines, copy routers and end milling machines; a hydraulic corner crimper, screwing and sash assembly machines, portable machines and conveyors; and complete production groups for 40 to 220 windows a shift. The saws have their own page — upcut, double-head, bead and miter saws. Every machine is supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON. Below, each page in brief and every model in one table.

faq.q: What machines does a PVC window shop need?
faq.a: At the least a saw, a copy router for the hardware and drainage holes, a welder, a corner cleaner, an end milling machine for the mullions and a glazing bead saw — the six machines of the PVC single-head group, about 40 – 60 windows a shift. Double-head saws and welders double that; a 4-corner welder, CNC corner cleaner and 3-axis CNC take a shop past 200 windows a shift.

faq.q: What is different for aluminum windows?
faq.a: Aluminum frames are not welded but joined with corner cleats and crimped — on the SÇ 902 — and the profiles are cut on saws with cooling and hydro-check feeds, machined on copy routers or CNCs with cooled 18,000 rpm spindles and end-milled on the heavier SÇ 211S. The aluminum double-head group puts those machines together.
The same material: rigid PVC, called uPVC in Europe and vinyl in North America. Every machine on these pages that is marked PVC works on vinyl window and door profiles.

faq.q: Can you plan a complete shop?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us the windows and doors you make, the profile systems and the output you need; we propose the machines, a layout and the air and power supply — as in Plastmak's workshop plan — then install and commission the line and train your operators.

faq.q: Do you install the machines and train operators?
faq.a: Yes. Our technicians install and commission every machine anywhere in Canada, set it up for your profiles and train the operators; spare parts and tooling are supplied from Mississauga, ON, and we support every machine by video call.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
